newsitem.title: USA: Soldiers closest to Gulf War gas found ill-study.
newsitem.headline: Soldiers closest to Gulf War gas found ill-study.

text.p: U.S. soldiers who were close to Iraqi gas weapons believed blown up at the end of the 1991 Gulf War have more muscle and joint pains than those further away, according to a U.S. government study released on Tuesday.
It was the first official study to show U.S. troops were not only near the apparent explosions of Iraqi chemical weapons but that some might have been made sick by the explosions.
Dr. Kenneth Kizer, the Department of Veterans Affairs' undersecretary for health, reported the findings at a hearing by a House Government Reform subcommittee.

Kizer said the study was based on examination of 1,978 of the 21,799 U.S. soldiers that the Defense Department had said were within 50 km (31 miles) when U.S. troops blew up Iraq's Kamisiyah weapons dump, which contained sarin and mustard gas weapons, in March 1991.

Kizer said 81 of the U.S. soldiers "who have been identified as part of the on-site Kamisiyah demolition team have been diagnosed with musculoskeletal conditions at a higher rate than veterans who were further away."
He said the finding was preliminary and would require further research.
